messages.content:
Classify these policies:

1. Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment: AI systems must not be used for making clinical decisions, determining diagnoses or treatment plans, creating individualised care plans for named patients, or generating clinical entries directly into patient records. Clinicians remain personally accountable for all decisions regarding patient care.
2. Protected Health Information: No person-identifiable data may be input to public AI tools. No business-sensitive or confidential data processing. Combined details of a local area, a rare disease and a very young age may enable a patient to be identified — careful anonymisation assessment required.
3. Medical Professional Impersonation: AI systems must not replace professional judgment or act as if they are medical professionals. Clinicians remain responsible for all decisions regarding patient care.

response.concept_definition: AI systems cannot make clinical decisions, diagnoses, treatment plans, or individualised care plans.
response.justification: This policy falls under safety as it aims to prevent potential harm from AI systems making incorrect or inappropriate medical decisions.

response.concept_definition: No person-identifiable data or confidential business data can be input into public AI tools. Anonymisation of data is required.
response.justification: This policy focuses on protecting sensitive personal and business information, aligning with confidentiality concerns.

response.concept_definition: AI systems cannot replace professional judgment or impersonate medical professionals.
response.justification: This policy falls under safety as it ensures that AI systems do not overstep their bounds and potentially mislead patients or clinicians.
